solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Amazed to be missing a grand time in Hawaii

indicators.note: to be missing something is to lack it, so the following letters are taken away

blocks.note: aghast means struck with amazement or horror
taken as written
G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished at losing a thousand dollars while on holiday in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and G from AGHAST to leave HAST.
explanation.definitionFit: HAST is the abbreviation for Hawaii-Aleutian Standard Time, the time zone used in the islands.

clue.text: Initial letters from His Majesty help female attendant

blocks.note: the initials of His Majesty are H and M, spelt out in full as 'H and M'
to aid is to help

explanation.surface: A royal attendant is helped by being given the king's monogram.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to write out the phrase 'H and M' with the word AND spelt in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaid is a female servant who waits on a mistress, an archaic word for a personal maid.

clue.text: Being surrounded by water is great on the rocks

definitions.note: a participial phrase standing for an adjective

indicators.note: something on the rocks is wrecked or broken up, so its letters are scattered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Being stranded at sea is great fun until you are shipwrecked on the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Seagirt is a poetic adjective for land encircled by the sea, as an island is.

clue.text: Hear publicity sounding like criminal group?

indicators.note: we are told the words only resemble the result in sound, not in spelling

blocks.note: to hear a case in court is to try it, and publicity is an ad

explanation.surface: Listening to an advert that seems to come from gangsters.
explanation.walkthrough: Hear is meant in the courtroom sense: a judge hears, or tries, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a Chinese organised-crime syndicate, so a gang of criminals.

clue.text: Person regularly left off society A-list?

definitions.text: Person regularly left off society A-list?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept
something taken off is removed, so the letter for the preceding word is dropped from what follows

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word
S is the standard abbreviation for society
L is the abbreviation for left; this is the letter removed
taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps getting left off the guest list of the fashionable set.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO plus S plus A-LIST with its L removed gives PROSAIST; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since a dull person is unlikely to be on the A-list.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosaist is a writer of prose, and by extension a dull, unimaginative person who would not be invited by celebrities.

clue.text: First chief out of line

indicators.note: out of here means missing, so the letter for the next word is taken away

blocks.note: primal means chief or fundamental
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: The top official has stepped out of line.
explanation.definitionFit: Prima is Italian for first, as in prima ballerina, the leading female dancer.

clue.text: Go batting with tail — absolute pain around pavilion?

indicators.note: batting suggests hitting things about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is a dictionary abbreviation for absolute

explanation.surface: A cricketer goes in to bat at the tail end of the order and suffers agony near the pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: The pavilion is the outer ear (pinna), not the cricket clubhouse the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia is the medical term for earache, and the pavilion of the ear is its visible outer flap.

clue.text: Gentleman's to go up north for green bird

blocks.note: sir is the form of address for a gentleman
gang is the Scots verb for to go; up north points to Scotland

explanation.surface: A gentleman sets off for the north to look for a rare green bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up north' means the dialect word is Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirgang is the green magpie or jay of the Himalayas, a bird with green plumage.

clue.text: Nihilist in one demo, not the first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is excluded

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a protest march is a demo

explanation.surface: An anarchist turns up at a protest rally, but not leading it.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarch is an archaic word for an anarchist, one who rejects all authority, close to a nihilist.

clue.text: Trainee accepted as improved

indicators.note: something improved has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An apprentice has been taken on because their work got better.
explanation.definitionFit: A space cadet is a trainee astronaut, though the phrase is also slang for a dreamy person.

clue.text: One from Balmoral, companion of the King — no sign of Harry

indicators.note: a sign of something is just a trace of it, here its opening letter
no here means without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: a thane was a nobleman attending a Scottish or Anglo-Saxon king
first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A royal companion at Balmoral, with Prince Harry nowhere to be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal castle in Scotland, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tane is Scots for 'the one', as in 'the tane and the tither', so one in Scottish speech.

clue.text: Scottish bishop and sailor wandering from the right path

blocks.note: the Bishop of Aberdeen signs himself by the abbreviated name of his see
a rating is a sailor without a commission

explanation.surface: A Scottish churchman and a seaman both stray from the straight and narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishops sign with the name of their see; Aber is the short form for Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: To aberrate is to deviate or stray, so aberrating means going astray from the correct course.

clue.text: Utter poise needed for dancing such?

definitions.text: Utter poise needed for dancing such?

indicators.note: letters that are dancing are moving about into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Complete balance is required to perform certain ballet moves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer: perfect balance is what spinning on one foot demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirouettes are ballet spins on one foot, which need great poise and balance to execute.

clue.text: Italian boat used by navy to store a thick fabric

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: barca is Italian for a boat
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: An Italian vessel is used by the fleet to stow heavy cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracan, or baracan, is a thick, coarse cloth originally from the Levant.

clue.text: Police officer's spirited second marriage

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector; the 's means 'is', joining the parts
gamy means spirited or plucky

explanation.surface: A detective is lively at his second wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Digamy is the act of marrying again after a first spouse dies or a divorce, a remarriage.

clue.text: Grumble about replacing parking for flight

indicators.note: one letter takes another's place in the word, the first named standing in for the second

blocks.note: to gripe is to grumble
c. (circa) means about
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone moans about having to swap a parking space for a plane trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight looks like air travel but means a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Grice is an old word for a step or flight of steps, also spelt grece or gree.

clue.text: Fellow leaving company rebuffed a scan

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the first word departs from the word for company
to rebuff is to send back, so what is left is read backwards

blocks.note: a firm is a company
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A colleague quits the firm after being refused a hospital scan.
explanation.definitionFit: An MRI is a magnetic resonance imaging scan, used to picture the inside of the body.

clue.text: Day with cops for Aberdeen rugby game?

definitions.text: Day with cops for Aberdeen rugby game?

indicators.note: a cop is the top or head of something, so the tops of the following words are taken

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A day out with the police at a rugby match in Aberdeen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a day's work, Aberdeen style. 'Cops' are heads, not police.
explanation.definitionFit: Darg is a Scots and northern word for a day's work or a set task.

clue.text: WI fruit cake put out last on table

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder
only the final letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A West Indian fruit cake is set out last of all on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: WI stands for West Indies, not the Women's Institute.
explanation.definitionFit: The ackee is a tropical fruit tree whose fruit is a staple of Jamaican cooking, in ackee and saltfish.

clue.text: Note, term for this: "stone" I fancy

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so the closing letter of the next word is taken
fancy suggests imaginative elaboration, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: E is a musical note
final letter of the word
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer notes the technical term for a gem they particularly admire.
explanation.walkthrough: The word stone does double duty, as part of the letters to rearrange and as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Essonite is cinnamon stone, a yellowish-brown variety of grossular garnet used as a gem.

clue.text: School orations on failing could make you tense

indicators.note: failing here means absent or lacking, so that short word drops out
to school is to train or discipline, so the letters are drilled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Speeches at school that go wrong could leave you nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like nervous, but it is the grammatical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorist is a past tense in Greek grammar, expressing simple past action.

clue.text: Rather effeminate relative getting rise for working

indicators.note: the letters are worked over, like dough being kneaded into a new shape

blocks.note: sis is short for sister
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather soft family member gets a pay rise for doing the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Sissier is the comparative of sissy, meaning more girlish or less tough.

clue.text: Produce call for a Marxist to be deselected?

blocks.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a type of Marxist
someone deselected is out

explanation.surface: Party members demand that a hard-left candidate be dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry 'Trot out!' is the call for removing a Trotskyist.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot out is to bring forward or produce something, usually tiresomely familiar, like an excuse.

clue.text: Bound by ceasefire, very good time for Corps

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter stands in for another

blocks.note: crucial is slang for excellent or very good
T is the abbreviation for time
C is the abbreviation for Corps

explanation.surface: An army unit enjoys a very good time once a truce is agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Trucial describes the Gulf states bound by the 1853 maritime truce with Britain, the Trucial States.

clue.text: Offhand about limits of test showing up yellowish oxide

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other
in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: airy means casual or offhand
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone casual about the boundaries of an exam reveals a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttria is yttrium oxide, a powder used in phosphors and ceramics, sometimes yellowish-white.

clue.text: Greek markets previously reckless, curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the final letter is docked

blocks.note: ago means in the past, previously
rash means reckless

explanation.surface: The Greek markets were once wild but have since been reined in.
explanation.definitionFit: An agora was a public square and marketplace in an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Reported extremely stupid reductions in size

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by speech, so we go by the sound

blocks.note: dense means very stupid, thick

explanation.surface: News stories call cuts to a company remarkably foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a dent in something is to reduce it, so dents are reductions in an amount.

clue.text: This beast loves the extremes of Indian desert?

definitions.text: This beast loves the extremes of Indian desert?

indicators.note: extremes are the far ends, here the closing letter of each of the next two words

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An animal that thrives in the harshest conditions of the Thar desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a camel loves the hostile desert of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Oont is Anglo-Indian army slang for a camel, from the Hindi word.

clue.text: Veteran eyes fish in Nova Scotia

definitions.note: plural noun; veteran signals an old word

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: NS is the postal abbreviation for Nova Scotia
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An old soldier spots fish in Canadian waters.
explanation.walkthrough: Eyes are not organs of sight: an eye is an old word for a brood of pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: A nide is a nest or brood of pheasants, the same thing as an eye or nye.

clue.text: Greens defending energy sector principally? Makes money for some in Asia

indicators.note: to defend is to shield or surround, so one piece is placed within the other
principally means first and foremost, so the opening letter is used

blocks.note: greens and tin are both slang for money
E is the symbol for energy
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners protect the energy industry, which earns a fortune in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Greens look like the political party, but are slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Teins are small coins of Kazakhstan, a hundredth of a tenge, so currency used in parts of Asia.

clue.text: Game long forgotten in Japanese plant

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so that letter disappears

blocks.note: ludo is a board game
L is the abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: A board game abandoned long ago in a Japanese garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludo is a simple board game played with dice and counters.
explanation.definitionFit: Udo is a Japanese aralia whose shoots are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Neat figures with zero entered for one

definitions.note: neat is a collective noun for cattle, standing for a plural

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, entered instead of it

blocks.note: stats are statistics, figures
zero looks like the letter O
a means one

explanation.surface: Tidy numbers with a nought written in place of a one.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat looks like tidy but is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Stots are young bullocks or steers, and neat is an old word for cattle.

clue.text: Forecast for Perth: flood with temperature dropping

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so that letter is lost

blocks.note: a spate is a river in flood
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: The weather outlook for Perth: floods, but temperatures falling.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Scottish town, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: To spae is the Scots verb meaning to foretell or prophesy.

clue.text: Join end of yarn to quantity of cloth?

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: a piece is a fixed length of cloth
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A weaver ties the loose end of a thread to a bolt of material.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'to' places the letter after the piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To piecen is a textile-mill term for joining broken threads in spinning.

clue.text: Pointer put out to show part of skull

indicators.note: put out suggests something displaced or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gun dog is shown off, displaying its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The pterion is the region of the skull where the frontal, parietal, temporal and sphenoid bones meet.

clue.text: Press alongside posh lodger and officer

blocks.note: to lie is to press, as in snow lying heavy
U means upper-class, posh
a lodger is a tenant

explanation.surface: Journalists sit beside a well-to-do lodger and an army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alongside' just sets the pieces next to each other. U for posh comes from the old U and non-U distinction in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a junior commissioned officer in the army or navy.

clue.text: Grasses lead in endless arguments outside the Bull

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is used
outside means surrounding, so one piece goes around the others

blocks.note: first letter of the word
to spar is to argue, so spars are arguments
T is an abbreviation for the
the bull on a dartboard is its centre, a circle like an O

explanation.surface: Endless rows about grazing land, with a bull in the middle of it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' is not about cutting: it is just the word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Mediterranean grass used for making paper and rope.

clue.text: Large number in New York drunk, bar closing

indicators.note: bar means except, so the closing letter is excluded

blocks.note: slued is American slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Plenty of people in New York are drunk by closing time at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a pub but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Slue is a variant spelling of slew, an informal word for a great quantity.
